question.leadin: Answer these questions about the native peoples of the Americas.
question.text: This civilization, with capital at Cuzco and another city at Macchu Picchu, was conquered by Francisco Pizarro.
question.clue: The language Quechua was spoken by members of this empire, and Hiram Bingham rediscovered one of its cities.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about colonial explorers who met violent ends.
swap.text: The conquistador Francisco Pizarro, who conquered this empire, was killed in a violent attack orchestrated by Diego de Almagro II. Pizarro himself had this Andean empire's ruler Atahualpa executed in 1533.
swap.clue: This empire's capital city, Cuzco, was captured by the conquistador Francisco Pizarro.

question.leadin: Tupac Amaru's 1572 uprising could not reverse the fate of this empire.
question.text: Identify this empire that was weakened by the civil war between the sons of Huayna Capac.
question.clue: One ruler of these people allegedly gained a fortune from places termed the "Outer Belt" and the "Fire Belt," and another earned a name meaning "overturner of the world" or "earthshaker" after stones supposedly came to life to help him repel Chanka invaders.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about old world writing systems.
swap.text: The Incan empire made use of this writing system which consisted of strings made from llama hair. The strings in this system were usually tied into knots.
swap.clue: Evidence for a writing system in these objects include a three-number sequence possibly representing the village of Puruchuco (poo-roo-CHOO-koh).

question.leadin: The Gate of the Sun was built by one culture centered around this body of water.
question.text: Name this body of water on the Altiplano. The ancestors of the Aymara people founded Tiwanaku on the shore of this lake.
question.clue: A civilization centred on this body of water created the Akapana mud pyramid and Pumapunku mounds, as well as a monolithic "Gate" that depicted 32 humans and 16 condor-headed people surrounding a central figure.

swap.text: The Chavin and later Andean civilizations made good use of this domesticated beast of burden which resembles a large alpaca.
swap.clue: The English word "jerky" derives from a term for the meat of these animals, charki.

question.leadin: These people identify with the ancient Tiwanaku culture, and they overran the Uru people of Lake Titicaca.
question.text: Name this indigenous people of the Altiplano region. Along with the Quechua people, they protested against natural gas development in their country in 2005.
question.clue: The katarismo movement which has sought to empower this group since the 1970s is named for the husband of martyr Bartolina Sisa.

swap.text: This city was the capital of the Inca Empire. Pachacuti remodeled this city and expanded its holdings to form the Inca Empire.
swap.clue: A chief of this puma-shaped city adopted a name roughly translated as "world turner."

question.leadin: Answer the following about remote sensing and the usage of aerial technology in archaeology.
question.text: While flying, Paul Kosok realized that what he believed were irrigation canals in a desert were actually animal-shaped lines, named for this civilization of southern Peru.
question.clue: Paul Kosok and Maria Reiche (RAI-keh) mapped structures created by these people.

swap.leadin: Atoc had his head turned into a goblet and his skin used as a drum after this war.
swap.text: Name this war in which Quisquis and Chalcuchimac led forces that defeated Huascar at the Battle of Quipaipan. The winner of this war would later be garroted despite filling a room with half a billion dollars in gold.
swap.answerHtml: Incan Civil War [accept Incan Dynastic War or War of the Two Brothers]
swap.clue: The winning side in this war employed the skilled generals Quizquiz and Chalcuchimac.

question.text: Drystone walls are well preserved in this Incan site, high in the Andes mountains that was unknown to Europeans until the 19th century.
question.clue: Hiram Bingham ("HEE-rum BING-hum") publicized the existence of this site.

swap.text: Quipus were often stored at stations known as tambos, where these messengers of the Inca would stop to relay information to other carriers.
swap.clue: This messengers who traversed the Qhapaq Nan ("KA-pak NYAN") to deliver messages in the form of knotted strings, or quipu ("KEE-poo").

question.leadin: Answer some stuff about the geography of Ecuador.
question.text: This high active volcano sits just south of Quito and destroyed the city of Tacunga in 1698 with an eruption.

swap.text: This emperor of the Inca wrote special hymns for the Situa Festival. This man, whose name means "Earthshaker," pacified the Chanca peoples and his son, Tupo Inca, built the Saqsaywaman Fort in Cusco.
swap.clue: This ruler, who legendarily subjugated the (+) Chanka people with stone warriors, organized his realm into four suyus.

question.text: In one timeline of the pre-Columbian Andean region, a period denoted "Early [this word]" contains the Chavin culture. In archaeology, this non-stratum word refers to a layer of distinctive material from a specific time period.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about black conquistadors.
swap.text: The mixed-race Juan Garcia held a post as town crier in this Peruvian city after participating in Pizarro's conquest of the Inca Empire, during which Atahualpa was captured in this city led by a lord who collaborated with the Spanish.
swap.clue: This city. A battle named for this city allegedly began after that aforementioned ruler threw down a Bible presented to him by Vincente de Valverde.

question.text: Further south, warfare with the Incas would certainly involve facing this prestigious general, who defeated Huascar at Quipaipan before losing to the Spanish at Vilcaconga and Maraycalla. He was killed by a mutiny in 1534 afer attempting to build resistance against Spain from a mountain stronghold.
question.clue: A man with this name failed to capture the town of Jauja from the Spanish shortly after being defeated by them at the Battle of Cusco.

swap.leadin: The artwork of this culture shows a spider god called the "Decapitator" holding a knife and a severed head, an indication that these people practiced human sacrifice.
swap.text: Name this civilization whose adobe temple at Huaca del Sol near Cerro Blanco is considered by many to be the largest pre-Columbian structure in South America.

question.leadin: This system was instituted by the Spanish in 1573 to draft people to work the mines of Potosi.
question.text: Identify this form of labor tax which used by the Incans for such infrastructure projects as the construction of the extensive network of roads.
question.clue: Las Casas would likely not have approved of the Spanish adoption of this Incan labor system which allowed them to conscript natives for public service work.

swap.leadin: They were put forth by the namesake Count of Oropesa and overturned the New Laws of Blasco Nunez Vela.
swap.text: Name this set of structural changes put forth in the 1570s, which created "reductions" of native population governed by kuraka, and established the mita system for forced labor in the silver mines.
swap.clue: Spain revived the mita system in this series of late 16th-century laws, which installed Inca regional leaders called kurakas as the head of repartimientos, or groups of natives from whom labor could be levied.
